eng.1.title: Omar Marmoush hails Luca Williams-Barnett as 'unbelievable' after full Spurs debut
eng.1.desc: Omar Marmoush has hailed Luca Williams-Barnett as "unbelievable" and believes the teen sensation has a "very promising future ahead of him." The 18-year-old scored one, and set up another, on his full debut for Tottenham in their 2-0 home win against Ipswich last weekend. Williams-Barnett has since signed a new deal to commit his future to Spurs until 2031. "He is unbelievable," Marmoush said of the Tottenham academy graduate. "He is a great, great talent and what I like most about him, of course his talent is something that everyone sees, is that he is very brave, too.

eng.1.title: FA panel details 'obvious error' in Leny Yoro red card against Liverpool
eng.1.desc: Referee Sam Barrott made an "obvious error" in sending off Manchester United defender Leny Yoro against Liverpool, an independent regulatory commission unanimously concluded. Yoro was shown a red card for bringing down Reds striker Alexander Isak as he raced towards goal early in Sunday's match at Anfield, although there has been significant debate over whether the Swede's heavy touch meant goalkeeper Senne Lammens would get to the ball before him.
eng.1.caption: Leny Yoro was shown a red card for his challenge on Alexander Isak in Manchester United's loss to Liverpool.

eng.1.title: Viktor Gyökeres: Arsenal not wasting energy on Man City's possible sanctions
eng.1.desc: Viktor Gyökeres said Arsenal cannot afford to waste any energy on Manchester City's possible sanctions -- as he vowed to deliver back-to-back Premier League titles for the Gunners. Arsenal will lock horns with City at the Emirates Stadium on Sunday for the first time since their rivals were found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations in September. City, who finished runners-up to Arsenal last season and are six points behind them heading into this weekend's mouth-watering contest, have appealed the verdict to leave the race for the title in limbo.

eng.1.title: VAR review: Why Man United should've gotten winner vs. Sporting
eng.1.desc: VAR often causes controversy, but how are decisions made? Our resident ref, Andy Davies, explains all. The video assistant referee causes controversy every week, whether it be the Premier League, Champions League or FA Cup, but how are those decisions made and are they correct? eng.1.title: Man United's costly errors overshadow early progress under Mauricio Pochettino
eng.1.desc: Manchester United showed signs of progress under Mauricio Pochettino, but familiar mistakes cost them a Champions League win against Sporting CP. LISBON, Portugal -- Mauricio Pochettino must wonder what he has walked into. Just a week and two games into his role as Manchester United head coach, he will have learned already that chaos is never far away. His plan for Liverpool on Sunday went out the window when Leny Yoro was controversially sent off after just eight minutes.

eng.1.title: Andoni Iraola: Alexander Isak in a 'great moment' after brace vs. Club Brugge
eng.1.desc: Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola believes striker Alexander Isak is in a "great moment" after he scored twice in the 3-0 victory over Club Brugge. Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola said he believes striker Alexander Isak is in a "great moment" after he scored twice in the 3-0 victory over Club Brugge. The Sweden international opened the scoring for the visitors in Belgium before Florian Wirtz doubled their advantage in the second half. Isak netted again in the 82nd minute to seal the win, taking his tally for Liverpool up to 10 goals for the season in all competitions. "He's in a great moment right now," Iraola said in his postmatch news conference.

eng.1.title: Nottingham Forest boss Glasner hits out at players who don't learn English
eng.1.desc: Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner said standards at the club were not good enough when he took charge. Forest have won just two of their 11 Premier League games since Glasner took charge this summer, becoming the club's fifth head coach in less than a year. "Stability in a company is having standards," Glasner told a news conference on Wednesday. "Everybody who joins commits to the standards. I think, very honestly, the standards were not high enough. "We have players who are here for four years, [who] can't speak English. If you go to Italy, after three months, every player gives his interview in the Italian language.

eng.1.title: Newcastle owners not considering full sale, only minority deals - reports
eng.1.desc: Newcastle's Saudi owners are not treating the possibility of selling a minority stake in the club as the first step towards a full sale, the Press Association understands. The Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF), which owns a majority stake in Newcastle, is understood to have enlisted JP Morgan to examine ways to fund the building of a new stadium. One method to achieve this could be the sale of new shares in the club, with The Athletic reporting that could equate to a new investor holding up to 25% of the club's shares and diluting the PIF's stake.

eng.1.title: Man City told regulator 'has the stomach' to challenge owners after charges
eng.1.desc: The chair of the Independent Football Regulator says his organisation "has the stomach" to take on Manchester City's owners should it need to. The IFR has the power to force directors off boards and even to force owners to divest from clubs in the most serious cases where they are found to be unsuitable. City have been found guilty of breaching Premier League rules over a nine-season period by an independent commission. The verdict, published in September, found they clearly intended to circumvent league rules through a series of "sham" arrangements which inflated revenues and disguised losses.

eng.1.title: Man United crisis: How did it start? Who is to blame? Is Pochettino the answer?
eng.1.desc: Struggling Manchester United find themselves in a familiar place and fans are getting tired of the cycle repeating itself. But can Mauricio Pochettino find the answer, or do the issues run deeper? There was certainly a logic to Manchester United's decision to hire former USMNT boss Mauricio Pochettino; the crisis got so deep that any option beyond a "safe pair of hands" gradually slipped out of the equation. Indeed, with the club second from bottom in the Premier League and facing the real threat of relegation, an experienced manager capable of restoring order and credibility was the only sensible appointment.

eng.2.title: Ryan Reynolds pays tribute as key assistant behind Wrexham's rise announces exit
eng.2.desc: Ryan Reynolds has paid tribute to Wrexham assistant manager Steve Parkin, who is set to leave the club after playing a key role in their remarkable rise from non-league to the Championship. Parkin, who joined Wrexham in July 2021, has been at manager Phil Parkinson's side throughout the Hollywood-owned club's three successive promotions. The 61-year-old will leave after Saturday's home game against Portsmouth, as he steps away from football to spend more time with his family. "My time at Wrexham has been truly special. While the three promotions have been unforgettable achievements, it is the relationships that I will treasure most.

eng.2.title: Burnley set English league record with 24th home game without a win
eng.2.desc: Burnley set a new record for the longest home run without a league win as Birmingham reaffirmed their Sky Bet Championship promotion credentials with a 2-0 victory at Turf Moor thanks to August Priske's strike and Jaydon Banel's own goal.
eng.2.credit: Martin Rickett/PA Images via Getty Images

eng.2.title: Scott Parker on West Ham's defeat at Portsmouth: 'Little bit groundhog'
eng.2.desc: Scott Parker has said his first victory as West Ham boss feels "close but so far" after a loss at Portsmouth extended his winless start to four games. Parker replaced Nuno Espírito Santo in the Hammers dugout earlier this month but has managed only two points so far, with the east Londoners on a six-game run without a win. West Ham failed to score for the first time this season against Portsmouth and, although they hit the woodwork twice, Parker did not consider his team unlucky. Parker said: "It was a little bit groundhog -- we had our chances today, but my overall feeling is that it is close but so far.
eng.2.caption: Scott Parker's West Ham team are sliding down the Championship table.

eng.2.title: Wrexham extend unbeaten run with draw at Bristol City
eng.2.desc: Bristol City stopped the rot at home by claiming a welcome point in a 1-1 draw with Wrexham. City boss Michael Skubala had to endure chants about his employment prospects from the Ashton Gate faithful after Joe Worrall had given Wrexham a seventh-minute lead. Cameron Pring rewarded the Robins' endeavour with a rare goal after 51 minutes, the full-back on target for the first time since December 2023. Wrexham are now unbeaten in four games, but they stay 14th and may well consider this an opportunity lost after making such a strong start.

eng.2.title: Late Thomason strike powers Wrexham to much-needed away win
eng.2.desc: George Thomason grabbed a late winner as Wrexham secured a welcome 1-0 victory away at Lincoln. It was a game lacking real quality in the final third at Sincil Bank, but Thomason kept his cool when the moment arose to fire Wrexham to victory with his 82nd-minute strike. It was a first away league victory for Phil Parkinson's side since the start of September when they beat Millwall 2-0. The Red Dragons have now gone three games without defeat and will be hoping to use their recent upturn in form as a catalyst towards their playoff push.

eng.2.title: Tony Mowbray steps back from Blackburn job due to health issues
eng.2.desc: Tony Mowbray has stepped back from his head coach duties at Blackburn due to health issues. Mowbray was diagnosed with bowel cancer in 2024 and had to stand down from his role at Birmingham but was given the all-clear and after a spell at West Brom last year, he joined Blackburn for a second spell in June. However, a statement from Rovers on Tuesday said health issues meant he was stepping away from work. "I'm immensely proud of this group of players. Their dedication and professionalism have given us some memorable performances and wins, and I've loved working with them," Mowbray said.

eng.2.title: Football regulator: EFL, National League clubs must hold financial reserves
eng.2.desc: EFL and National League clubs will be compelled to hold financial reserves relative to their level of risk by the Independent Football Regulator (IFR). Clubs deemed to be at high risk of running into financial difficulty by the IFR will be required to hold the equivalent of five months' operating losses in reserve, dropping to two months for those deemed medium risk. Low-risk clubs will be required to hold one month's wages, the IFR said, as it opened a six-week consultation on reserves on Tuesday. There will be no fixed requirement on Premier League clubs, the IFR said, but they will be assessed on a case-by-case basis.

eng.2.title: Tom Brady leaves Birmingham with club top of Championship
eng.2.desc: Tom Brady has left Birmingham City, the Championship club has confirmed, as it thanked the NFL legend for his "unwavering support." Brady became a minority owner with a 3.3% stake and chairman of a newly created advisory board in August 2023 with the seven-time Super Bowl champion quarterback entering into a partnership with Birmingham's owners, Knighthead Capital Management LLC, headed by his friend and business partner Tom Wagner. Birmingham had an eventful few years while Brady was at the club as they hired England and Manchester United legend Wayne Rooney as head coach before sacking him 83 days later.

eng.2.desc: Socceroos midfielder Alex Robertson has been feted as "Kangaroo" by his Cardiff City teammates after he bounced back from scoring an own goal to lash home a sensational, stoppage-time winner in one of the Championship side's greatest comebacks.

eng.2.title: Wrexham boss on Ryan Reynolds, Rob Mac: 'Uplifting' when they come to watch
eng.2.desc: Wrexham couldn't serve up a blockbuster for owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac but manager Phil Parkinson praised the Hollywood duo's input into a point that kept Wolves off the Championship summit. Lewis O'Brien brought the A-listers to their feet with a first goal of the season to cancel out Adam Armstrong's latest strike two minutes earlier. Kieffer Moore missed a chance to win it for the Welsh side in the second half but Red Dragons' goalkeeper Anthony Patterson produced several big saves to deny Wolves victory at the Racecourse since a first meeting in 1924.

eng.2.title: Ryan Reynolds, Rob Mac watch on as Wrexham deny Wolves top spot with draw
eng.2.desc: Lewis O'Brien's first goal of the season earned Wrexham a 1-1 draw and prevented Wolves going top of the Championship, under the watching eye of Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac. Wolves have never won at the Racecourse Ground but Adam Armstrong's latest strike after 25 minutes suggested they might register a history-making victory. Instead, O'Brien equalised for Phil Parkinson's side two minutes later though the visitors still extended their unbeaten run to six matches. Wrexham co-owners Reynolds and Rob Mac were in attendance for only this seventh league meeting between the sides in 102 years and first since 1988.

eng.2.title: Wrexham joy at big win dented by losing striker Sam Smith for season
eng.2.desc: Wrexham's morale-boosting win over Championship leaders Middlesbrough was partially overshadowed by confirmation that striker Sam Smith will miss the rest of the season. Wrexham 's morale-boosting 2-0 win over Championship leaders Middlesbrough was partially overshadowed by confirmation that striker Sam Smith will miss the rest of the season after suffering an anterior cruciate ligament injury. Smith suffered the injury during Wrexham's 1-0 defeat at Sheffield United on Friday. The 28-year-old had previously started all 13 of Wrexham's league games this season.
eng.2.caption: Wrexham's Sam Smith is set to miss the rest of the season after suffering a serious knee injury against Sheffield United.

eng.2.title: West Ham snatch draw from 3-0 down in Scott Parker's first game in charge
eng.2.desc: Scott Parker saw his West Ham side recover from three goals down to draw 3-3 at Cardiff in a thrilling first game in charge. Jack Moylan's first hat trick in English football had Cardiff in cruise control at halftime and Hammers fans venting their anger. But the Hammers -- inspired by captain Jarrod Bowen -- fought back in incredible fashion as Divine Mukasa, Arne Engels and Max Kilman netted to secure a point. Parker was confirmed as Hammers boss on Wednesday morning -- just 24 hours after Nuno Espirito Santo's departure -- but it was a tough watch for the former England midfielder initially as Moylan had Cardiff 3-0 ahead inside 39 minutes.

eng.2.caption: Scott Parker applauds the fans.

eng.2.title: Wrexham beat top-of-table Middlesbrough to end losing skid
eng.2.desc: Championship leaders Middlesbrough suffered only their second league defeat of the season as Wrexham eased the pressure on Phil Parkinson with a much-needed 2-0 win on Wednesday. George Thomason rifled Wrexham in front in the 71st minute and substitute Oli Rathbone sealed it with an 84th-minute header to give Wrexham only their fourth win of the season, coming after back-to-back defeats against Blackburn and Sheffield United left the Red Dragons hovering just above the drop zone.
eng.2.caption: Wrexham players celebrate after scoring a goal against Middlesbrough in the Championship.

eng.fa.title: FA Cup manager sent off for headbutting rival player before extra-time winner
eng.fa.desc: A manager who oversaw an FA Cup upset was sent off for headbutting a player on the opposing side. Micky Mellon was no longer on the touchline to see his Oldham Athletic side complete an extra-time victory against Sheffield Wednesday because he had been red carded. In the 84th minute, manager Mellon pushed his head towards Wednesday midfielder Callum Slattery and was given his marching orders. Slattery was booked after a touchline fracas was calmed down. League Two Oldham eventually dumped League One Wednesday out of the famous cup competition after a 2-1 win, with Will Sutton's 110th-minute winner.

eng.fa.title: Notts County beat Altrincham in FA Cup amid severe fog: 'Couldn't see the ball or players'

esp.1.title: Barcelona to appeal Fermín López's two-match ban - sources
esp.1.desc: Fermín López has been hit with a two-match suspension after getting sent off in Barcelona's comeback win against Villarreal last weekend. Fermín, 23, will miss Barça's LaLiga fixtures at Deportivo A Coruña this weekend and the home game against title rivals Atlético Madrid next Wednesday. esp.1.title: Diego Simeone takes LaLiga win record with 345th Atlético Madrid victory
esp.1.desc: Diego Simeone has become LaLiga's all-time record holder for wins as a manager after Atlético Madrid strolled to a 3-0 victory at Getafe on Sunday. The Argentinian reached 345 victories -- all with the Madrid club -- surpassing the record set by former Atlético, Barcelona and Spain manager Luis Aragonés between 1974 and 2004. Simeone reached the milestone in 567 matches, giving him a 60% win rate during his 15 years in LaLiga. "This is not a trophy, but it is an important number as a coach," Simeone said in a news conference after Sunday's win.

esp.1.title: USMNT's Cardoso scores as Atlético ease to win over Getafe
esp.1.desc: Atlético Madrid bolstered their spot in third in LaLiga with a comfortable 3-0 win at Getafe on Sunday. A superb long-range strike by Álex Baena put Diego Simeone's team in front and Johnny Cardoso's 30th-minute tap-in increased Atlético's stranglehold on the contest in Madrid. Getafe pushed for a way back into the contest, but Atlético stood firm and grabbed a third late on from the penalty spot via Alejandro Grimaldo to make it eight wins in nine league matches. It took Atlético only 10 minutes to break the deadlock when Julián Álvarez controlled inside the area and teed up Baena, who let fly from 30 yards and found the bottom corner.

esp.1.desc: Villarreal have denied that Nicolas Pépé underwent eye surgery as a result of viewing the solar eclipse. The Ivorian winger missed five games in October after undergoing the surgery, but the LaLiga club have refuted reports that this was due to viewing the phenomenon without the proper protection. Such reports surfaced after footage on social media -- allegedly posted by Pépé himself -- appeared to show the former Arsenal man looking directly at the eclipse on Aug. 12, 2026, without a solar viewer.

ita.1.title: Lazio are top of Serie A despite playing without their fans
ita.1.desc: Lazio's success this season has been one of the big stories in Serie A, made more remarkable by the fact that their fans won't attend home games until the club is sold. We're approaching the end of November and Lazio are top of Serie A, with 32 points in 12 games. The last time it happened was more than 25 years ago and back then, soccer -- and Lazio -- were entirely different animals.
